2 · An answer: no change (shown for the phone layout)

Real recorded answer for "Is paying pregnant smokers to quit worth the cost?" (the limitation line is made up for the mockup; the source card is shortened here and works as today). Nothing new under the answer.

  1. ✓Planning
  2. ✓Retrieving
  3. ✓Synthesizing
  4. ✓Checking claims

Becky's answer

Yes
  1. A cost-effectiveness analysis of a Glasgow RCT of up to £400 in incentives for pregnant smokers found an incremental cost of £1127 per cotinine-validated quitter at 34-38 weeks, and a lifetime model ICER of £482/QALY, well below a £30,000/QALY willingness-to-pay threshold.[1]
  2. The cost per quitter was similar to a standard look-up value from published ICER tables (£1390 per quitter), supporting the plausibility of the estimate.[1]

Limitations

  1. The analysis is based on a single trial in one city.[1]

Sources

Becky read 5 abstracts and used 1 of them.

    Supports findings 1–2 and limitation 1

4 · /eval: the gain from reading the abstracts, made bigger

Same numbers, same words. The two "vs closed-book" lines become large mint cards instead of small lines under the tiles.

1. Reading the abstracts is what makes the answers good

Share of the 200 test questions answered correctly (PubMedQA's own yes / no / maybe answers; a refusal counts as wrong).

Baseline (reads abstracts)76.5%153/200
Agent (reads abstracts)74.0%148/200
Closed-book (same AI, no abstracts)54.0%108/200

+22.5 pts baseline vs closed-book (95% range +15.0 to +29.5)

+20.0 pts agent vs closed-book (95% range +12.5 to +27.0)

Without the abstracts, the AI did no better than always answering "yes" (55.0%). Both gains are well clear of zero.

6 · Browser tests that will be added (Playwright, against the $0 fake backend)

  1. Answer: click an example, ask, see the verdict, numbered findings, limitations and source cards.
  2. Not enough evidence: see the shrug, the reason, the tips; tapping a tip question fills the box.
  3. Citation: clicking [2] opens source card 2, scrolls it into view, focuses it and plays the blue glow.
  4. Step list: the four steps tick in order (Planning → Retrieving → Synthesizing → Checking claims); when a step fails it shows ✕ and the later steps say "not started" (one run per failing step).
  5. Reduced motion: with the browser set to "reduce motion": Becky doesn't bounce, no page flip, the placeholder doesn't rotate, the citation jump is instant (no smooth scroll, no glow).
  6. /eval: the page loads with its numbers, the big gain cards and the Limitations section.
  7. Failures: server down, connection cut mid-answer, and the "demo limit reached" message.
  8. Phone width: every state above at 375 px with no sideways scrolling; the footer disclaimer is on both pages.

They run on every push to GitHub (frontend job). $0: no real AI calls; the fake backend answers.
